messages.content:
Number: 2
Title: Scope and application

Text:
2.1 This policy statement applies to all banks, building societies, payment institutions and electronic money institutions authorised by the FSOA.

2.2 It applies to the firm's activities in all jurisdictions where the failure of an activity could cause harm to consumers in our jurisdiction or to the stability of our financial system.

2.3 Some requirements are applied proportionately. For the purposes of this policy statement, a small firm is a firm that has fewer than 250,000 customers and total assets of less than £5 billion on 31 December 2026. A firm that exceeds either threshold is not a small firm.

2.4 A firm that becomes a small firm, or stops being a small firm, after 31 December 2026 must notify the FSOA within 30 days of the change. Its status for the purposes of the transitional arrangements in section 9 is fixed on 31 December 2026 and does not change.

2.5 Groups may meet these requirements at group level, provided that each authorised firm in the group can show how the group arrangements apply to its own important business services.

request.system:
# Section summariser agent
You are given one section: its number, title and text. Return a `SectionSummary` as a single JSON object, with no text before or after it:

- `number`: the section number, for example `"4"`.
- `title`: the section title.
- `summary`: one to three sentences on what the section says.
- `obligations`: every obligation in the section. Use an empty list if there are none.

Each `Obligation` has four fields:

- `requirement`: what the firm must do, in plain English.
- `paragraph`: the paragraph number it comes from, for example `"4.2"`.
- `deadline`: the deadline exactly as written in the document, or `null` if there is none.
- `evidence`: a quote copied word for word from that paragraph, at most 30 words.

For example:

```json
{
  "number": "7",
  "title": "Incident reporting",
  "summary": "Firms must report major incidents to the regulator quickly.",
  "obligations": [
    {
      "requirement": "Report major incidents to the regulator",
      "paragraph": "7.1",
      "deadline": "within 4 hours",
      "evidence": "Firms must notify the FSOA of a major incident within 4 hours"
    }
  ]
}
```

### What counts as an obligation

An obligation is something a firm must do. Look for "must", "shall", "is required to" and "will need to".

- Do not list recommendations or guidance ("should", "may", "we expect") as obligations.
- Do not list things only the regulator does.
- If one paragraph sets several separate requirements, list each one separately.
- If the section changes a requirement or deadline from an earlier section, say so in the summary.

### Rules for accuracy

- Copy `evidence` word for word. Never paraphrase, correct or shorten the wording inside a quote.
- Copy `deadline` exactly as written. Do not convert dates or durations, for example "within 4 hours" stays as it is.
- Use only the section you were given. Do not use outside knowledge of the regulation.
- Do not guess. If a paragraph is ambiguous, say so in the summary rather than inventing a requirement.

These fields are checked automatically against the source text afterwards. A quote that isn't word for word, or a
deadline that isn't in the section, will be flagged.

obligations.evidence: A firm that becomes a small firm, or stops being a small firm, after 31 December 2026 must notify the FSOA within 30 days of the change.
obligations.requirement: Notify the FSOA when the firm becomes, or stops being, a small firm after 31 December 2026

args.summary: The policy applies to banks, building societies, payment institutions and e-money institutions authorised by the FSOA, including activities in any jurisdiction where failure could harm consumers or financial stability. A small firm (under 250,000 customers and under £5 billion assets on 31 December 2026) gets proportionate treatment; firms must notify changes in status, though transitional status is fixed. Groups may comply at group level if each firm shows how this applies to its own important business services.
